areas.name: M&M wall (AKA "Supercave Wall")
areas.blurb: M&M Wall — better known as Supercave Wall — is a steep, south-facing granite wall rising above the North Cascades Highway (SR-20) about 2 miles northeast of Liberty Bell, roughly 3 miles east of Washington Pass. It is one of the largest and cleanest roadside crags in Washington, known for bulletproof granite and a mid-height system of huge caves (the largest "Supercave" is roughly the size of a tennis court). Long ignored after a single 1969 aid ascent, the wall saw almost no further traffic for 40 years until Erik Lawson and Lee Arden Pete established Ellen Pea (2009), followed by a wave of hard free climbing from Blake Herrington and partners (The Tiger, 2014; free variation of the L&H Route, 2015) and Colin Moorhead/Tom Wright (Golden Age, 2016).
